subject: medicine
title: Advanced Parkinsonian Therapies and Atypical Parkinsonism

steps.tx: Non-ergot synthetic compounds that directly stimulate striatal dopamine D2 and D3 receptors independent of presynaptic neuronal degeneration are **dopamine agonists** (such as pramipexole and ropinirole). Primarily utilized as initial monotherapy in younger onset Parkinson patients or adjunctive therapy with levodopa, they carry a high risk of neuropsychiatric impulse control disorders (pathological gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping).

steps.tx: With advancing disease and progressive loss of striatal presynaptic dopamine storage capacity, patients develop motor fluctuations where the therapeutic benefit of a levodopa dose shortens to under three to four hours. Termed the **wearing-off** phenomenon, patients alternate between functional mobility during on periods and severe bradykinesia and rigidity during off periods.
steps.say: With advancing disease and loss of striatal dopamine storage capacity, patients develop motor fluctuations where the therapeutic benefit of each levodopa dose shortens. Termed the wearing-off phenomenon, patients alternate between functional mobility during on periods and severe rigidity during off periods.

steps.tx: Fluctuating plasma levodopa concentrations also induce peak-dose involuntary choreiform and dystonic movements known as levodopa-induced **dyskinesias**. Management options include smoothing levodopa delivery using catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) inhibitors like entacapone, adding the NMDA antagonist amantadine, or evaluating patients for deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus.

steps.tx: Neurodegenerative conditions that share parkinsonian features but fail to respond robustly to levodopa are designated as atypical parkinsonian syndromes. A 4-repeat tauopathy characterised by early postural instability, frequent backward falls within the initial year, and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy (impairing downward voluntary saccades) is **progressive supranuclear palsy** (PSP, Steele-Richardson-Olszewski syndrome).
steps.say: Neurodegenerative conditions that share parkinsonian features but fail to respond to levodopa are designated as atypical parkinsonisms. A tauopathy characterized by early postural instability, frequent backward falls, and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy is progressive supranuclear palsy.

steps.tx: An alpha-synucleinopathy characterised by prominent oligodendroglial cytoplasmic inclusions, profound autonomic failure (severe orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence, erectile dysfunction), and either cerebellar ataxia or parkinsonism is **multiple system atrophy** (MSA). MRI of the brain demonstrates characteristic midbrain hummingbird sign in PSP and pontine hot cross bun sign in MSA-C.
steps.say: An alpha-synucleinopathy characterized by oligodendroglial cytoplasmic inclusions, severe autonomic failure with orthostatic hypotension, and either cerebellar ataxia or parkinsonism is multiple system atrophy. Brain MRI shows the midbrain hummingbird sign in PSP and the pontine hot cross bun sign in cerebellar MSA.

steps.tx: The most common pathological movement disorder in adults is **essential tremor**, an autosomal dominant monosymptomatic tremor disorder. In sharp contrast to Parkinson disease, essential tremor is a high-frequency (eight to twelve Hertz) postural and kinetic action tremor affecting the bilateral upper extremities during active motor tasks (pouring water, writing) and head (titubation), completely lacking bradykinesia, rigidity, or resting tremor.
steps.say: The most common pathological movement disorder in adults is essential tremor, an autosomal dominant disorder. In contrast to Parkinson disease, essential tremor is a high-frequency postural action tremor affecting bilateral hands during motor tasks like writing, completely lacking bradykinesia or rigidity.

rows: Typically unilateral or asymmetrical at onset
Frequent yes-yes or no-no head titubation
No improvement with alcohol; responds to Levodopa

steps.tx: Secondary parkinsonism induced by pharmacological dopamine receptor blockade is a common iatrogenic mimic termed drug-induced parkinsonism. Typical first-generation antipsychotics (haloperidol, fluphenazine) and gastrointestinal prokinetic agents (metoclopramide) block striatal D2 receptors, precipitating acute **dystonia**, parkinsonian rigidity, akathisia (motor restlessness), and delayed tardive dyskinesias.
steps.say: Secondary parkinsonism induced by dopamine receptor blockade is a common iatrogenic mimic termed drug-induced parkinsonism. First-generation antipsychotics and prokinetics like metoclopramide block striatal D2 receptors, precipitating acute dystonias, rigidity, akathisia, and delayed tardive dyskinesias.

steps.tx: Surgical neuromodulation has revolutionized the management of medically refractory Parkinson disease with motor fluctuations. High-frequency electrical stimulation of the **subthalamic** nucleus (STN) or internal segment of the globus pallidus (GPi) via implanted deep brain stimulation electrodes normalizes aberrant basal ganglia output, dramatically reducing off-time, dyskinesias, and medication requirements.
